question: What are the working hours?
reference: Core hours are 10:00 to 16:00, Monday to Friday. The remaining hours are flexible as long as the week totals 40 hours.

question: Is overtime paid for?
reference: Overtime is not paid as money. It is compensated with time off in lieu, taken within 60 days, and only if a manager approved it in advance. The answer must say that approval is needed before the overtime is worked. Saying only "approved overtime" is not enough.

question: How many days can I take off?
reference: 20 days of paid annual leave per year, increasing to 25 after five years of service. The question is ambiguous, so a good answer may also mention sick leave (10 days) and public holidays (12 days), but these are optional.

question: Are my leaves carried forward if unused?
reference: Up to 5 unused annual leave days carry over to the next year and expire on March 31. Sick days do not carry over.

question: Do I have sick leave?
reference: Yes, 10 paid sick days per year. They do not carry over. A doctor's note is required for absences longer than 3 consecutive days.

question: Are sick leave and annual leave counted together?
reference: No. Sick leave is separate from annual leave and does not reduce it.

question: Is there any maternal leave in case of pregnancy?
reference: Primary caregivers get 16 weeks of paid parental leave, which must begin within 6 months of the birth or adoption. The handbook says nothing about leave during pregnancy, before the birth. The answer must give the 16 weeks AND say explicitly that leave before the birth is not covered. Saying only that there is no separate maternal leave policy is not enough.

question: What should I do if my laptop got damaged?
reference: Should say the handbook does not cover damaged laptops. May mention the lost or stolen rule (report to IT within 24 hours), but must not present it as the rule for damage.

question: What is the dress code?
reference: Should say the handbook does not cover the dress code. Must not invent a policy.

question: Can I work from my sofa all week?
reference: The employees can work remotely for upto 3 days a week, fully remote arrangements require approval from a department head and are reviewed every 6 months. Employees working remotely must be reachable during core hours. A home office stipend of 500 USD is available once, within the first 90 days of employment. Must not invent a policy.

question: Do I have to change my password regularly?
reference: No. Passwords are rotated only after a suspected breach, not on a fixed schedule. Extra details such as the 14-character minimum and mandatory multi-factor authentication are optional.

question: Can I give my password to IT if they ask for it?
reference: No. Employees must never share credentials, including with colleagues or IT staff.

question: If a public holiday falls on a Saturday, do I get Monday off?
reference: No. If a public holiday falls on a weekend, it is not moved to a weekday. The company observes 12 public holidays per year, which is optional detail.

question: Can I carry my unused learning budget into next year?
reference: No. Unused learning budget does not roll over. The budget is 1,200 USD per year. Optionally, conference travel is covered separately under the travel policy.

question: How often are performance reviews?
reference: Twice a year, in June and December. Optionally, each review covers the goals from the previous cycle and sets new ones, with written feedback from the manager.

question: Does the company offer a gym membership?
reference: Should say the handbook does not cover gym memberships. Must not invent a benefit, and must not present the learning budget or the home office stipend as a gym benefit.

question: What happens if I am sick for more than 10 days in a year?
reference: Employees receive 10 paid sick days per year, and a doctor's note is required for absences longer than 3 consecutive days. The handbook does not say what happens after the 10 days are used. A good answer gives the 10 days and says that what follows is not covered.

question: What is the most I can spend on a hotel in Tokyo?
reference: Hotel stays are reimbursed up to 180 USD per night in standard cities and 250 USD per night in high-cost cities such as New York, London, and Tokyo.

question: Do I get free money for a standing desk?
reference: There is a one-time home office stipend of 500 USD, available within the first 90 days of employment. The handbook does not say what the stipend covers, so it cannot confirm that a standing desk qualifies. A good answer mentions the stipend and says it is unclear whether a standing desk is covered.

question: Can I bring my dog to the office?
reference: The handbook does not cover this policy.

question: I am traveling for work, what can I claim and how fast?
reference: Hotel up to 180 USD a night in standard cities and 250 in high-cost cities, a daily meal allowance of 60 USD, and flights booked through the travel portal (economy under 6 hours). Claims must be submitted within 30 days, with a receipt for anything over 100 USD, and are paid with the next monthly payroll. Alcohol, client meals and flight class details are optional.

question: How long can I work from my house and when will I be reimbursed for my home office setup?
reference: Remote work is allowed up to 3 days per week; fully remote needs department head approval and is reviewed every 6 months. There is a one-time home office stipend of 500 USD, available within the first 90 days of employment. The handbook does not say how or when the stipend is paid, and the answer must say so. It must not present the expense claim rules (30 days, next payroll) as the way the stipend is paid. Being reachable during core hours is optional.

question: Will I get my own laptop and when is the perfomance review?
reference: Yes, every new employee gets a company laptop. Performance reviews happen twice a year, in June and December. Laptop replacement every 3 years, the other equipment rules and the review details are optional.

question: What is the policy for parental leave and what happens if I am sick for more than 10 days in a year?
reference: Primary caregivers get 16 weeks of paid parental leave and secondary caregivers 6 weeks; it must begin within 6 months of the birth or adoption. Employees get 10 paid sick days a year. The handbook does not say what happens after the 10 days are used, and the answer must say so. Splitting parental leave into two blocks and the doctor's note rule are optional.

question: Can I use my learning budget to go to a conference in London, and what will the hotel cost me?
reference: Yes: the learning budget of 1,200 USD per year covers conferences. Conference travel is covered separately under the travel policy, not from the learning budget. London is a high-cost city, so the hotel is reimbursed up to 250 USD per night; anything above that is paid by the employee. Booking through the travel portal and the flight rules are optional.
